stories.headline: Anthropic Hits $1 Trillion Valuation on Secondary Markets, Surpassing OpenAI's $880B on Forge Global

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's valuation on Forge Global, a leading private marketplace exchange, has hit approximately $1 trillion, surpassing OpenAI which trades at $880 billion on the same platform.
On Hiive, another secondary marketplace, Anthropic share prices surged 211% to roughly $900 over the past three months, while OpenAI shares rose only 8.5% to $608 in the same period.
The surge is driven by Anthropic's rapid revenue growth — from $9 billion at end of 2025 to over $30 billion by end of March 2026 — and strong adoption of Claude Code.

Glen Anderson, CEO of Rainmaker Securities, said he received an offer to buy Anthropic shares at a $960 billion valuation — 'an unthinkable price even just weeks ago.' A separate offer from a 'very well-known growth fund' came in at $1.05 trillion.
Anthropic's last primary funding round valued the company at $380 billion; the secondary market premium implies ~2.6x that valuation. OpenAI's last primary round was $852 billion.

stories.headline: Anthropic Publishes Postmortem on Claude Code Quality Drop: Three Bugs Fixed, Usage Limits Reset

key_facts.fact: Anthropic traced Claude Code quality complaints to three separate changes: reduced default reasoning effort (March 4), a caching bug that cleared thinking every turn (March 26), and a system prompt limiting responses to ≤25 words between tool calls (April 16).

The reasoning effort change reduced default from 'high' to 'medium' to cut latency; Anthropic called it 'the wrong tradeoff' and reverted on April 7. All users now default to 'xhigh' for Opus 4.7 and 'high' for other models.

The caching bug was meant to clear old thinking from idle sessions once, but instead cleared it every turn, making Claude 'forgetful and repetitive.' It passed multiple layers of review before being caught.
The verbosity-reduction system prompt caused a measurable 3% drop in coding benchmarks for both Opus 4.6 and 4.7, and was reverted on April 20. All issues resolved in v2.1.116.
As compensation, Anthropic reset usage limits for all subscribers. The company also set up the @ClaudeDevs X account for more transparent communication of product decisions.
Anthropic is adding tighter controls: broader per-model eval suites for every system prompt change, soak periods, gradual rollouts, and new tooling to make prompt changes easier to review and audit.

stories.headline: Applied Digital Lands $7.5B 15-Year Lease for 300MW AI Data Center With US Hyperscaler

key_facts.fact: Applied Digital signed a 15-year lease with an unnamed US investment-grade hyperscaler for 300MW of capacity at its Delta Forge 1 campus, worth approximately $7.5 billion in total contracted value
The deal expands Applied Digital's total contracted lease revenue to over $23 billion, with more than 50% now backed by investment-grade customers
Delta Forge 1 is a 430MW AI Factory campus in the southern United States designed for AI and high-performance computing workloads
Applied Digital shares rose 9-14% intraday on the announcement, reflecting investor enthusiasm for long-term AI infrastructure demand

stories.headline: AI Coding Startup Cognition in Early Funding Talks at $25B Valuation, Up From $10.2B in September

key_facts.fact: Cognition AI is in early talks to raise hundreds of millions of dollars or more at a $25 billion valuation, more than doubling its $10.2 billion valuation from September 2025.
Cognition is best known for Devin, which the company bills as an autonomous AI software engineer that automates code creation, debugging, and deployment. Customers include Dell and Cisco.
The company acquired Windsurf in July 2025 and annual recurring revenue has more than doubled since that acquisition. Devin's ARR grew from $1M in September 2024 to $73M by June 2025.
The funding talks were already underway when SpaceX announced its $60 billion deal for Cursor, adding fuel to AI coding valuations.

stories.headline: Cohere Acquires Germany's Aleph Alpha in $20B Sovereign AI Deal, Schwarz Group Invests $600M

key_facts.fact: Canadian AI startup Cohere agreed to acquire German AI startup Aleph Alpha in a deal valuing the combined entity at approximately $20 billion. Cohere shareholders receive ~90% of the combined company, Aleph Alpha's ~10%.
Schwarz Group, which owns retailers Lidl and Kaufland, will invest $600 million in Cohere's upcoming Series E round as part of the deal. Cohere was last valued at $6.8 billion in August 2025.

Global HQ stays in Toronto, European HQ in Berlin. Cohere CEO Aidan Gomez remains CEO. Germany's Digital Minister Karsten Wildberger and Canada's AI Minister Evan Solomon attended the Berlin announcement.

The deal targets sovereign AI for regulated sectors — public sector, finance, defense, energy, healthcare — giving Cohere access to Aleph Alpha's existing German government contracts including the ministry for digital affairs.
Cohere CFO Francois Chadwick told Reuters: 'We are going to commit to working with European infrastructure and maintain the sovereignty requirements that are being addressed in Europe.'

stories.headline: Cohere and Aleph Alpha Merge Into $20B Transatlantic AI Company for Sovereign AI

key_facts.fact: Canada's Cohere and Germany's Aleph Alpha agreed to merge into a combined entity valued at approximately $20 billion, intended as an alternative to US AI providers for governments and enterprises.

Cohere shareholders will receive approximately 90% of the combined entity and Aleph Alpha shareholders ~10%, making it effectively a Cohere acquisition. CEO Aidan Gomez will lead the combined company.

The combined company will have its global headquarters in Toronto and its European headquarters in Berlin. Germany's Digital Minister Karsten Wildberger and Canada's Evan Solomon attended the announcement.
Aleph Alpha backer Schwarz Group will invest $600 million in Cohere's upcoming Series E funding round.
The German government is set to become an anchor customer of the merged entity as part of a broader European push for digital sovereignty and reduced dependence on US tech giants.

stories.headline: Cursor Hit $2.7B Annualized Revenue in March, Up 14x YoY, as Gross Margins Turn Positive

key_facts.fact: Cursor hit $2.7 billion in annualized revenue in March 2026, 14 times higher than a year ago. Investors expect annualized revenue to exceed $7 billion by year-end.
Cursor's gross margins have turned positive after being at -23% in January 2026, helped by cost structure optimizations and the launch of the Composer model.

Cursor recently agreed to a potential $60 billion acquisition by SpaceX, or a $10 billion collaboration fee. SpaceX isn't acquiring immediately due to its imminent IPO targeting a $2 trillion valuation.

Cursor had been days from closing a separate $2 billion funding round at a $50 billion valuation when the SpaceX deal halted those talks. Microsoft had also looked at a Cursor acquisition before SpaceX moved and chose not to proceed.
Cursor pays retail prices to Anthropic and OpenAI — the same companies competing against it with Claude Code and Codex. SpaceX's compute infrastructure would restructure those unit economics.

stories.headline: DeepSeek Releases V4-Pro (1.6T Params) and V4-Flash, Largest Open-Source Models With 1M Context

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek-V4-Pro has 1.6T total parameters with 49B active (MoE), pre-trained on 33T tokens. V4-Flash has 284B total with 13B active, trained on 32T tokens. Both support 1M token context.
V4-Pro is the largest open-weights model released, bigger than Kimi K2.6 (1.1T) and GLM-5.1 (754B), and more than twice the size of DeepSeek V3.2 (685B).
V4-Pro API pricing is $1.74/1M input tokens and $3.48/1M output; V4-Flash is $0.14/1M input and $0.28/1M output — the cheapest in both model tiers.
DeepSeek says V4-Pro trails state-of-the-art frontier models (GPT-5.4 and Gemini 3.1-Pro) by approximately 3 to 6 months, and is the strongest open-source model in coding and math benchmarks.
V4 introduces a hybrid attention mechanism (Compressed Sparse Attention + Heavily Compressed Attention) that reduces KV cache to 10% and single-token FLOPs to 27% of V3.2 at 1M context.
Both models are open-sourced under the MIT license on Hugging Face. The release was timed to coincide with OpenAI's GPT-5.5 launch on the same day.

Huawei announced its Ascend supernode based on the Ascend 950 AI chips will fully support DeepSeek V4. DeepSeek says V4-Pro throughput is currently limited by high-end compute supply, with prices expected to drop when Huawei Ascend 950 super nodes ship at scale in H2.

stories.headline: EU Approves €90B Loan for Ukraine and 20th Sanctions Package After Hungary Lifts Veto

key_facts.fact: The EU approved a €90 billion ($106 billion) loan package for Ukraine to cover economic and military needs for the next two years, after Hungary lifted its veto.
Russian oil resumed flowing through the Druzhba pipeline to Slovakia after a three-month halt, removing the key obstacle to Hungary and Slovakia lifting their veto.

The 20th sanctions package targets Russian energy revenues, shadow fleet, crypto, and military-industrial complex, banning transactions with 20 Russian banks and imposing a sectoral ban on Russian crypto providers.
46 additional vessels were banned (total: 632), and the EU activated its anti-circumvention tool for the first time, restricting exports to Kyrgyzstan over re-exports of sanctioned goods to Russia.
The sanctions include expanded export bans worth €360M+ and import bans worth €570M+, covering lab glassware, lubricants, chemicals, metals, and minerals.
16 entities in third countries (China, UAE, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Belarus) face sanctions for supplying dual-use goods or weapons to Russia.

stories.headline: Huawei Says Ascend 950 SuperPod Fully Supports DeepSeek V4, Achieves 20ms Inference Latency

key_facts.fact: Huawei announced its entire Ascend SuperPod product line now supports the DeepSeek V4 series models, following the V4-Pro and V4-Flash open-source release
The Ascend 950 SuperPod achieves low-latency inference of 20ms for DeepSeek V4-Pro and 10ms for DeepSeek V4-Flash, redefining performance ceiling for long context inference
DeepSeek V4-Pro has 1.6 trillion total parameters with 49 billion active, trained on 33 trillion tokens with a 1 million token context window, released under MIT license
Alibaba, ByteDance, and Tencent have purchased hundreds of thousands of Ascend 950PR chips for cloud services to sell DeepSeek models; prices of the chip have risen 20% due to demand
DeepSeek V4 also supports Cambricon chips as an alternative to Huawei's Ascend, diversifying China's domestic AI chip ecosystem

stories.headline: Intel Q1 Revenue Beats by 9% at $13.6B as Data Center Jumps 22% and Foundry Grows 16%

key_facts.fact: Intel Q1 2026 revenue was $13.58 billion, up 7.2% YoY and well above the $12.42 billion analyst estimate; adjusted EPS was $0.29 vs $0.01 expected
Data Center and AI segment revenue rose 22% YoY to $5.1 billion, driven by Xeon CPU demand and 10-15% server CPU price increases
Intel Foundry revenue was $5.4 billion, up 16% YoY, though external foundry revenue was only about $170 million (~3% of total)
Q2 guidance of $13.8-14.8B revenue and $0.20 adjusted EPS exceeded analyst estimates of $13.07B and $0.09 respectively

Intel shares surged 15%+ after hours; the stock has risen more than 80% this year, with CEO Lip-Bu Tan citing the shift from foundational models to inference and agentic workloads as driving CPU demand
Google signed a multi-year contract to use Xeon CPUs for AI inference and other workloads; latest PC and data-center chips are being produced on the 18A process at a new Arizona plant

stories.headline: Meta Cuts 8,000 Jobs and Closes 6,000 Roles as AI Capital Spending Hits $135B

key_facts.fact: Meta will lay off approximately 8,000 employees (10% of workforce) on May 20 and close 6,000 open roles, bringing the effective headcount reduction to 14,000 positions.

The layoffs were announced in an internal memo by CPO Janelle Gale, who said they are part of 'our continued effort to run the company more efficiently and to allow us to offset the other investments we're making.'
Meta's guided capital expenditure for 2026 is $115B to $135B, a 73% increase over the $72.2B spent in 2025, largely directed at AI infrastructure.
Additional job cuts are planned for H2 2026; if the second wave matches the first, Meta will have eliminated roughly 20% of its pre-2026 workforce.
Meta also told employees earlier this week that a new tracking tool will capture keystrokes and mouse movements from work computers to train AI agents.
CEO Mark Zuckerberg said on Meta's January earnings call that 2026 would be 'the year that AI starts to dramatically change the way that we work.'

stories.headline: Nokia Q1 Profit Jumps 54% as Optical Networks for AI Data Centers Drive €1B in Hyperscaler Orders

key_facts.fact: Nokia's Q1 2026 comparable operating profit was €281 million, up 54% YoY; shares rose 7% in Helsinki to their highest level since 2010, up 63% year-to-date
Optical networks segment grew 20% in Q1, the fastest of all Nokia divisions; Nokia secured about €1 billion in new orders from hyperscalers including Amazon, Google, and Microsoft
Revenue exposure to AI and cloud customers expanded to 8% of total and rose 49% YoY as hyperscalers build large-scale AI training infrastructure
Nokia raised its 2026 network infrastructure growth guidance from 6-8% to 12-14%, driven by optical and IP networks demand from AI customers
Nokia forecasts the AI and cloud-related network market will grow at a 27% CAGR through 2028, nearly double last year's forecast

stories.headline: OpenAI Launches GPT-5.5 With Gains in Agentic Coding and Computer Use, Priced at $5/$30 Per 1M Tokens

key_facts.fact: GPT-5.5 released April 23, six weeks after GPT-5.4. It scores 82.7% on Terminal-Bench 2.0, beating Claude Opus 4.7 (69.4%) and Gemini 3.1 Pro (68.5%). On OSWorld-Verified it scores 78.7% vs Claude Opus 4.7 at 78.0%.
On SWE-Bench Pro (real GitHub issue resolution), GPT-5.5 scores 58.6%, while Claude Opus 4.7 scores 64.3% — Anthropic still leads in production coding.
API pricing is $5/1M input tokens and $30/1M output tokens — double GPT-5.4. GPT-5.5 Pro costs $30/1M input and $180/1M output. Both have a 1M token context window.
OpenAI claims GPT-5.5 uses ~40% fewer output tokens for equivalent tasks, bringing the effective net cost increase to around 20% despite the doubled per-token price.
Rolling out to Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users in ChatGPT and Codex. GPT-5.5 was co-designed and trained on Nvidia's GB200 and GB300 NVL72 systems.

GPT-5.5 matches GPT-5.4 per-token latency in real-world serving despite higher capability. OpenAI leads the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with a score of 60, three points ahead of Claude Opus 4.7 and Gemini 3.1 Pro at 57.

stories.headline: China's Pudu Robotics Raises ~$150M at $1.5B+ Valuation, Opens US HQ in Texas

key_facts.fact: Pudu Robotics raised nearly $150 million in a new funding round, bringing cumulative funding past $300 million and valuation above $1.5 billion
The company achieved 100% year-over-year revenue growth in 2025, with commercial cleaning now representing over 70% of total revenue
Pudu holds 23% global market share in commercial service robotics according to Frost & Sullivan, ranking first worldwide; customers include Carrefour, Walmart, and EDEKA
Pudu relocated its US headquarters from Santa Clara to Richardson, Texas, with nearly 15,000 robots deployed across the Americas and ambitions to serve one million US users in five years
Industrial delivery robots saw rapid adoption with over 4,000 units shipped within one year of market launch; funds will accelerate embodied AI technologies and manufacturing capacity

stories.headline: FDA Approves Regeneron's Otarmeni, First Gene Therapy for Genetic Hearing Loss, Free in the US

key_facts.fact: The FDA granted accelerated approval for Otarmeni (lunsotogene parvec-cwha), the first gene therapy for genetic hearing loss and the first FDA-approved gene therapy to restore a neurosensory function to normal levels.
In the CHORD trial, 80% of the 20 evaluable pediatric patients achieved or surpassed the primary hearing endpoint at week 24, and with longer follow-up, 42% achieved normal hearing.
Regeneron will make Otarmeni available for free in the United States and announced a drug pricing deal with the White House.

OTOF-related hearing loss is ultra-rare, affecting 20-50 newborns per year in the US. Otarmeni delivers a functioning OTOF gene to inner ear hair cells via an infusion into the cochlea under general anesthesia.

The FDA approved Otarmeni just 61 days after Regeneron submitted its biologics license application, making it the sixth approval under the National Priority Voucher program and the first for a gene therapy.
Regeneron acquired Decibel Therapeutics, which originally developed the therapy (then called DB-OTO), in 2023 for up to $213 million including milestones.

stories.headline: TerraPower Begins Construction on First Next-Gen Nuclear Plant in the US, a 345MW Natrium Reactor

key_facts.fact: TerraPower officially started construction on Kemmerer Unit 1 in Wyoming on April 23, the first utility-scale advanced nuclear power plant in the United States
The NRC construction permit issued in March 2026 was the first for a commercial non-light water reactor in more than 40 years and the first for any commercial reactor in nearly a decade
The Natrium plant features a 345MW sodium-cooled fast reactor with molten salt thermal storage that can boost output to 500MW for over 5 hours during peak demand
The project is backed by up to $2 billion in cost-shared federal support through DOE's Advanced Reactor Demonstration Program; founded by Bill Gates
TerraPower aims for nuclear fission reactor operational by end of 2030; about 1,600 workers during construction and 250 permanent once operational
TerraPower already has an agreement with Meta to build 8 Natrium reactors in the US, with the first two intended to come online in 2032

stories.headline: Trump Threatens 'Big Tariff' on UK If It Doesn't Drop Its 2% Digital Services Tax

key_facts.fact: Trump told reporters at the White House that the US will 'put a big tariff on the UK' if Britain does not drop its digital services tax, which he views as unfairly targeting American tech companies like Apple, Google, and Meta.
The UK's 2% digital services tax, introduced in 2020, generated £944 million in the 2025-26 fiscal year (up 17% YoY) and is projected to raise £1.4 billion annually by 2030.
The warning comes ahead of King Charles III's state visit to the US next week; Trump said the monarch could help repair Washington's relationship with Britain, which has become strained.

Trump said: 'I don't like it when they target American companies, because basically, you're talking about our great American companies... We've been looking at it, and we can meet that very easily by just putting a big tariff on the UK.'

The DST has been criticized by both Trump and his predecessor Joe Biden. The UK has so far resisted Washington's calls to drop the tax, maintaining it ensures digital businesses contribute fairly based on their economic activity in the country.

stories.headline: US Accuses China of Industrial-Scale AI Distillation; Beijing Orders Tech Firms to Reject US Capital

key_facts.fact: White House OSTP Director Michael Kratsios wrote in a memo that the US has intelligence indicating 'foreign entities, principally based in China' are conducting 'industrial-scale distillation' of American AI models using tens of thousands of surrogate accounts.

The White House plans to share intelligence with US AI companies, coordinate private-sector defenses, develop best practices, and explore measures to hold foreign actors accountable for distillation campaigns.

In a parallel move, Chinese regulators including the NDRC told tech firms such as ByteDance, Moonshot AI, and StepFun to reject US capital without state approval, responding to Meta's acquisition of Chinese AI startup Manus.

The House Foreign Affairs Committee advanced bipartisan export control bills on April 22 that would close loopholes allowing China to access US AI technology, including considering listing distillation entities on the Entity List.

Anthropic has previously accused DeepSeek, Moonshot, and MiniMax of conducting distillation attacks against Claude; OpenAI has made similar accusations against DeepSeek for using GPT outputs to train its models.

The dual escalation came weeks before a planned Trump visit to Beijing, with China's embassy responding that its AI development 'is the result of its own dedication and effort as well as international cooperation.'

stories.headline: DOJ Arrests US Soldier for $400K+ Polymarket Insider Bet on Maduro Capture He Helped Plan

key_facts.fact: Gannon Ken Van Dyke, a 38-year-old Army special forces soldier at Fort Bragg, was charged with wire fraud, commodities fraud, and theft of nonpublic government information — the first criminal case in the US tied to prediction market wagers.

Van Dyke participated in the planning and execution of the January 2026 predawn raid that captured Maduro, then bet approximately $33,034 across 13 wagers on Polymarket that Maduro would be removed from power, earning over $409,000 in profits.
The CFTC separately filed a civil complaint seeking restitution, disgorgement, trading bans, and a permanent injunction against further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act.
Van Dyke faces up to 20 years in prison if convicted of the top count (wire fraud) and up to 10 years on each remaining count.

Trump, when asked about the arrest, said: 'The whole world, unfortunately, has become somewhat of a casino.' Trump's son Donald Jr. is both an investor in Polymarket and a paid adviser to rival Kalshi.
Israeli authorities in February arrested several people and charged two on suspicion of using classified information to place bets about military operations in Iran on Polymarket.

stories.headline: Zhongji Innolight Breaks 1 Trillion Yuan Market Cap as AI Optical Module Demand Surges

key_facts.fact: Zhongji Innolight's stock crossed ¥900/share on April 23, pushing its market cap past the 1 trillion yuan (~$146B) mark and ranking 13th on the A-share market
The stock surged over 12x in one year, from ¥66.86/share in March 2025 — the fastest journey from 100 billion to 1 trillion yuan market cap in A-share history
Q1 2026 revenue reached ¥19.5 billion ($2.7B), up 192% YoY, with net profit of ¥5.7 billion, up 262%
Broker estimates indicate Zhongji Innolight holds roughly 80% of Nvidia's 1.6T optical module procurement and over 40% of the global 800G market
Morgan Stanley built a major position worth ¥3.7 billion in Q1 2026, entering the top-10 shareholders; Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and Temasek also invested
